title: Sridevi
wiki_lead:
Sridevi Kapoor (née Shree Amma Yanger Ayyapan; 13 August 1963 – 24 February 2018), known mononymously as Sridevi, was an Indian actress who worked in Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, Malayalam, and Kannada language films. Cited as the "first female superstar" of Indian cinema, she was the recipient of various accolades, including a National Film Award, Seven Filmfare Awards (a Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award, Three Filmfare Awards, Three Filmfare Awards South),  Tamil Nadu State Film Awards, a Kerala State Film Award, and a Nandi Award. Sridevi's career spanned over 50 years in a wide range of genres. She was known for her reticent and introverted off-screen personality, but headstrong and outspoken on-screen persona, often playing strong-willed women. In 2013, Sridevi was honoured with the Padma Shri, the country's fourth highest civilian honour.
Sridevi made her debut as a child in the 1967 Tamil film Kandhan Karunai at the age of four, and began playing lead roles as a child in M. A. Thirumugam's 1969 mythological Tamil film Thunaivan. Her first role as an on-screen adult came in 1976 at age 13, in the Tamil film Moondru Mudichu. She soon established herself as a leading female star of South Indian Cinema, with roles in such films as 16 Vayathinile (1977), Sigappu Rojakkal (1978), Padaharella Vayasu (1978), Varumayin Niram Sivappu (1980), Meendum Kokila (1981), Premabhishekam (1981), Vazhvey Maayam (1982), Moondram Pirai (1982), Aakhari Poratam (1988), Jagadeka Veerudu Athiloka Sundari (1990) and Kshana Kshanam (1991).
Sridevi's first starring role in Hindi cinema came with the drama film Solva Sawan (1979), and she received wider recognition for the action film Himmatwala (1983). She emerged a leading Hindi film star with several successes, including Mawaali (1983), Justice Chaudhury (1983), Tohfa (1984), Maqsad (1984), Karma (1986), Mr. India (1987), Waqt Ki Awaz (1988) and Chandni (1989). She received praise for her performances in Sadma (1983), Nagina (1986), ChaalBaaz (1989), Lamhe (1991), Khuda Gawah (1992), Gumrah (1993), Laadla (1994), and Judaai (1997). Following a hiatus, she played the title role in the television sitcom Malini Iyer (2004–2005). Sridevi returned to film acting with the comedy-drama English Vinglish (2012) and had her 300th and final film role in the crime thriller Mom (2017). She earned acclaim for both performances, and for the latter was posthumously awarded the National Film Award for Best Actress.
On 24 February 2018, she was found dead in her guest room at the Jumeirah Emirates Towers Hotel in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, with the cause cited as accidental drowning. News of her death featured prominently in Indian and international media. She was married to film producer Boney Kapoor, with whom she had two daughters, actresses Janhvi and Khushi Kapoor.

grok_lead: Sridevi (13 August 1963 â 24 February 2018), born Shree Amma Yanger Ayyapan, was an Indian actress and producer renowned for her versatile performances across Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, Malayalam, and Kannada cinema over a career spanning five decades and more than 300 films. Widely regarded as the first female superstar of Bollywood, she dominated the industry in the 1980s and 1990s with iconic roles that blended comedy, drama, and action, earning her the moniker "first lady of Indian cinema" and establishing her as one of the highest-paid actresses of her era. Sridevi began her acting journey as a child artist at the age of four, debuting in the 1967 Tamil devotional film Kandhan Karunai, followed by her first lead role in the 1976 Tamil film Moondru Mudichu. Her breakthrough came in South Indian cinema with critically acclaimed performances in films like Moondram Pirai (1982, Tamil), where she portrayed a woman with retrograde amnesia, earning widespread praise for her emotional depth. Transitioning to Hindi cinema, she made her adult lead debut in Solva Sawan (1979) and quickly rose to prominence with blockbusters such as Himmatwala (1983) and Tohfa (1984), captivating audiences with her expressive dance sequences and multifaceted characters. At the peak of her career in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Sridevi delivered memorable performances in films like Mr. India (1987), where she played the journalist Seema, showcasing her comic timing and overshadowing the male lead; ChaalBaaz (1989), for which she won the Filmfare Award for Best Actress in a dual role; Chandni (1989), a romantic drama that became a cultural phenomenon; and Lamhe (1991), noted for its bold exploration of intergenerational love. After a 15-year hiatus from acting to focus on family, she staged a triumphant comeback with English Vinglish (2012), playing a middle-aged woman learning English, which resonated globally and highlighted her enduring appeal. Her final film, Mom (2017), featured her as a vengeful mother and marked her 300th project. Sridevi's accolades include three National Film Awards for Best Actressâfor Moondram Pirai (1982), English Vinglish (2012), and posthumously for Mom (2017)âalong with five Filmfare Awards and the Padma Shri in 2013 for her contributions to cinema. In her personal life, Sridevi was born in Sivakasi, Tamil Nadu, to a Tamil father, Ayyappan, a lawyer, and a Telugu mother, Rajeswari, from Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh; she had a younger sister, Srilatha. She married film producer Boney Kapoor in 1996, and the couple had two daughters, Janhvi and Khushi Kapoor, both of whom later entered the film industry. Sridevi passed away suddenly on 24 February 2018 in Dubai due to accidental drowning following a cardiac arrest, at the age of 54, leaving behind a profound legacy as a trailblazer who challenged gender norms in Indian cinema and inspired generations of actors. Posthumously, she received honors including a special tribute at the 2018 Cannes Film Festival and the Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award in 2019.
